record.context_brief: Fredholm failure of the L2 exponential map
record.original_question: For a compact Riemannian three-manifold M, can one quantify how the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) fails to be a Fredholm map, for example by measuring the noncompact part of the operator that appears in its derivative?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian three-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the Hilbert manifold of Sobolev-class $H^s$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, for $s > 5/2$. Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric, whose geodesics correspond (by Arnold's theorem) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e : T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity $e$.

It is known that, in contrast to the two-dimensional case where $d\exp_e$ at each point decomposes as the sum of an invertible operator and a compact operator (so that $\exp_e$ is a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero), in dimension three the corresponding "compact part" $K$ appearing in the derivative $d\exp_e$ generally fails to be compact, so $\exp_e$ fails to be Fredholm.

Problem. Quantify the failure of the $L^2$ exponential map $\exp_e$ on $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ to be a nonlinear Fredholm map. For instance, provide a natural measure of the noncompact part of the operator $K$ appearing in $d\exp_e$ (such as its essential spectrum, essential norm, distance in operator norm to the compact operators, or membership in suitable Schatten–von Neumann or other operator ideals as a function of the initial velocity field), and describe how this quantity depends on the geometry of $M$ and on the initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: The qualitative result that the $L^2$ exponential map on volume-preserving diffeomorphisms is Fredholm in 2D but generically fails to be Fredholm in 3D (with the relevant operator not even Hilbert–Schmidt) is established in works by Ebin–Misiołek–Preston and follow-ups. However, no published quantitative measure of how badly Fredholmness fails in 3D (e.g. essential norm, Schatten-class membership, or essential spectrum of the compact-part operator) appears in the literature; recent work (e.g. on singular sets of Riemannian exponential maps in hydrodynamics, 2025) still treats this as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Fredholm properties of Riemannian exponential maps on diffeomorphism groups
status_evidence.snippet: The compactness operator belongs to Schatten classes p>2 in 2D but the failure of compactness in 3D is essential.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that Fredholmness of the L2 exponential map fails essentially in dimension three, without giving a quantitative measure.

status_evidence.title: Singular sets of Riemannian exponential maps in hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies singular structure of exponential maps on diffeomorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work continuing to investigate singularities/Fredholm structure of these exponential maps, indicating the quantitative question remains active.

status_evidence.title: Normal Forms for the L2 Riemannian Exponential Map on Diffeomorphism Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Normal forms in cases where Fredholm property holds.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses normal-form theory under Fredholmness but does not quantify failure in 3D.
